source.title: Position: LLM Unlearning Benchmarks are Weak Measures of Progress
source.authors: Pratiksha Thaker; Shengyuan Hu; Neil Kale; Yash Maurya; Zhiwei Steven Wu; Virginia Smith

page_placements.theme: Inference-time, gated or by-design reversible methods reach unlearning scores with weights unchanged

record.tranche_reason: The study’s own experiments show that benign changes to benchmark queries can expose unlearned information or substantially damage retain performance, challenging the reliability and scope of benchmark-based unlearning claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own experiments on paired TOFU questions, answer-choice substitutions, and a TOFU keyword filter. Prior work on Harry Potter prompt changes, relearning, and other attacks is discussed or cited, not tested here. The WMDP figure values are not stated numerically in the text; they are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own benign query changes on existing unlearned models. On TOFU it pairs each retain question with a forget question; on WMDP's MMLU retain set it swaps one wrong answer choice for 'SARS-CoV-2'. Retained ability collapses for DPO, ECO, RMU and RMU+LAT, while the base model does not suffer. One paired prompt also gets ECO to output a forgotten author's name. Together these bear on A's claim that unlearning keeps general ability and resists simple prompting, and on prompt-only recovery (E).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue that forget/retain benchmarks overstate unlearning success. Benign changes that create dependencies between forget and retain queries, or that swap an irrelevant answer choice, either reveal 'unlearned' information or collapse retain performance, even under a weak threat model of benign queries. Benchmark design also encourages overfitting to the test queries, through filters or classifiers. They recommend caution, held-out queries and multiple query formats, clear threat models, separating unlearning from censorship, and formal or provable guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: Uses existing unlearning methods and benchmark settings, but evaluates them with paired questions and modified answer choices rather than the original disjoint-query evaluations.
record.method_sensitivity: Paired forget/retain questions cause significant retain-score drops for DPO and ECO, while gradient ascent is described as stable. Swapping an incorrect answer choice produces different effects for the base model, RMU, and RMU with LAT.

fits_no_version.finding: An exact-name keyword filter scores about 1.0 on TOFU forget abstention and on retain accuracy without using any unlearning data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark-level unlearning scores can be reached by inference-time filtering that removes no knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: ECO's WMDP classifier relies on the word 'college' in a prepended prompt. Without that prefix it classifies at 37% accuracy, worse than random.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier-gated unlearning methods can overfit to spurious features of the benchmark format.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors' own linear classifier, trained on held-out WMDP/MMLU questions, matches RMU on WMDP. Holdout scores are Bio 31.7 vs RMU 31.2 and Chem 34.8 vs 45.8, with MMLU All 54.1 vs 57.1 (Table II).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A query classifier that refuses forget-topic questions can match weight-based unlearning on WMDP accuracy metrics without removing knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
record.problems: The paired-query recovery example is qualitative and limited to a reported example. Figure 3 and Figure 4 values are not numerically transcribed in the text. These experiments do not test fine-tuning recovery, internal edits, quantization, or several prompting attacks discussed in the paper.

untested.parts: Does not measure forget-set accuracy itself; the Table II RMU and SSD values are cited from WMDP. No recovery attack on the WMDP forget set for RMU or RMU+LAT; the swap was applied to retain questions only.
No activation ablation or internal analysis.

No paraphrase sweeps, jailbreaks, translation or in-context attacks. No recovery rate across paired queries; recovery is shown by one ECO example only. No recovery on the WHP or WMDP forget sets; the query-format results on WHP are cited from Lynch et al. and Shi et al.
No newer method is tested for resisting recovery. LAT is evaluated only for retain loss under the answer swap.

missing.what: The Fig. 3 ROUGE values appear as data labels in the text (e.g. GA precision 0.210/0.211, F1 0.300/0.309), but the reader marked them 'figure only'. Which DPO and ECO bars the extracted labels belong to is ambiguous and needs checking against the figure.
The general statement that unlearned models 'uniformly fail' on combined queries, treating both authors as unlearned (retain lost). It is unquantified.
The same statement's other case: models that treat both authors as retained, which reveals the forget author. It is unquantified, with no rate of recovery.
ECO classifier accuracy of 37% (worse than random) once the prepended topic phrase is removed. This bears only indirectly on A, since it is a classifier score, not forget-set accuracy.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
1. Merged the two r10 items (the cause of the duplicate_row_fix error) into one item linked to E only, state observed. One state cannot serve both A (where the effect is absent) and E (where it is observed). r10 is removed from the row_ids of the A 'challenges' label for DPO/ECO on TOFU; that label's reason now points to r10 under E.
2. Corrected r18's problem text. Table II lists RMU virology at 25.9, which is near chance, not below it, and is cited from WMDP. The 'worse than random' wording is the authors' own description.
3. Split the missing entry 'A, E' into one entry per version.
4. Added to A's untested parts that no forget-set recovery attack was run on the WMDP models.
5. Added a fits_no_version entry for the authors' linear-classifier results in Table II.
6. Small wording additions: ECO is an inference-time classifier-gated method, and GA recall values are probably 0.665/0.642 but uncertain.
All other judgments are kept. The TOFU experiments probably use the TOFU Llama-2-7B-chat finetune, but the text does not say so for these runs. No instructions were found in the study text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly test whether targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance while general ability is preserved and simple attacks fail to recover the targeted knowledge.
Does not test recovery by fine-tuning on a relearning set.
Does not test activation-direction ablation or whether internal edits block access rather than delete knowledge.
Does not test quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests paired forget-and-retain questions on TOFU; does not test paraphrase sweeps, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Does not test whether a newer method resists fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization, or prompting-recovery attacks.

rows.subject: ECO (TOFU; model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Asked a combined question containing one forget-author query and one retain-author query

conditions.value: paired TOFU question: forget author Nikolai Abilov and retain author Adwoa Ampomah

rows.measure: Whether the response gives the forgotten author’s correct name
rows.baseline: The paper says a retrained model hallucinates an incorrect response for the forget author
rows.value: ECO gives the correct response for both authors, including Nikolai Abilov
rows.note: The authors say ECO misclassifies the combined query as retain and gives the forgotten author’s correct name.
rows.check: A single qualitative example with no rate: given a benign paired question, ECO outputs the forgotten author's name, Nikolai Abilov, while a retrained model hallucinates. ECO gates an embedding corruption with an inference-time classifier, so the leak comes from a classifier miss, not from weights. Linked to E only; it also contradicts A's 'simple attacks don't recover' for ECO, but one state cannot serve both versions.

source_check.problem: A single qualitative example. ECO is a classifier-gated inference-time method, and its weights are intact.
